eventMetadata.context_description: **Traders have converged on a 35°C high for the official Seoul/Incheon station on August 6 because ongoing heatwave conditions, driven by a persistent high-pressure system and clear skies, are producing afternoon maxima tightly clustered around that threshold according to Korea Meteorological Administration forecasts and station observations.** Current readings near 36–37°C with low humidity and light winds support peak values in the mid-30s, consistent with the agency’s heatwave warnings that project daytime temperatures of 32–39°C across the region through early August. Historical climatology for early August in the Seoul metropolitan area shows average highs near 30–32°C, but this year’s anomalous warmth—following record-setting July peaks above 42°C—has shifted the distribution upward, making 35°C the most probable single outcome under current model consensus. Realistic challenges include a faster-than-expected sea-breeze intrusion from the Yellow Sea that could cap the high at 33–34°C, or a late-day cloud build-up reducing insolation enough to prevent the thermometer from reaching 35°C before the official daily maximum is recorded.
